records.source: וּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל׀לְֽמִסְפָּרָ֡ם רָאשֵׁ֣י הָאָב֣וֹת וְשָׂרֵ֣י הָֽאֲלָפִ֣ים׀וְהַמֵּא֡וֹת וְשֹׁטְרֵיהֶם֩ הַמְשָׁרְתִ֨ים אֶת־הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ לְכֹ֣ל׀דְּבַ֣ר הַֽמַּחְלְק֗וֹת הַבָּאָ֤ה וְהַיֹּצֵאת֙ חֹ֣דֶשׁ בְּחֹ֔דֶשׁ לְכֹ֖ל חָדְשֵׁ֣י הַשָּׁנָ֑ה הַֽמַּחֲלֹ֨קֶת֙ הָֽאַחַ֔ת עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֖ה אָֽלֶף׃ס
records.gloss: And [the] sons of Israel by their number, heads of the fathers and commanders of the thousands and the hundreds and their officers, who served the king in every matter of the divisions, the [one] coming in and the [one] going out month by month for all [the] months of the year: the division the one [was] twenty and four thousand.
pieces: This is the list of the Israelites by number: heads of families, commanders of thousands and of hundreds, and the officials under them, who served the king in every matter that concerned the divisions. One division came on duty and another went off duty month by month throughout the year, and each division had 24,000 men.

L.1: And the sons of Israel by their number, the heads of the fathers and the commanders of the thousands and of the hundreds, and their officials, who served the king in every matter of the divisions that came in and went out month by month, for all the months of the year: each division [was] 24,000.

R.1: Here is the list of the Israelites who served the king: the family leaders, the army commanders over units of a thousand and of a hundred, and their officials. They served the king in everything that had to do with the army divisions. Each division served for one month of the year, and then the next division took its place. There were 24,000 men in each division.

decisions.choice: the divisions: twelve army units, each on duty for one month of the year
decisions.reason: The word means a share or division. It is used for the divisions of the priests and Levites who served in turn (23:6; 24:1). Here the men of Israel who served the king are organized the same way: twelve divisions, each serving for one month (verses 2-15), so that the king always had a force on duty without calling up the whole people.

decisions.choice: coming in and going out month by month: taking up duty and leaving it in turn
decisions.reason: Coming in and going out is a common way of describing a period of service from start to finish (2 Kings 11:9). Each month one division came on duty and the one before it went home.

decisions.choice: thousands; 24,000: the word read as the number "thousand"
decisions.reason: As in the census lists, the word for "thousand" can also name a military or clan unit, which would make the divisions much smaller. The question is set out at Numbers 1:21 and applies to the figures in this chapter.

decisions.choice: the sons of Israel (Literal); the Israelites (Balanced, Readable), with no gender span
decisions.reason: The people listed here are the men who served in the king's army divisions, so the inclusive alternative used elsewhere for this phrase does not apply.

decisions.choice: had 24,000 men; One division came on duty and another went off duty
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say that the 24,000 were men, the soldiers of each division, and spell out the monthly turn of duty (m2).

decisions.choice: officials
decisions.reason: As at 23:4 and Deuteronomy 16:18: the word names the men who kept the records and carried out orders under the commanders.

records.heading: The army divisions

records.source: עַ֞ל הַמַּחֲלֹ֤קֶת הָרִֽאשׁוֹנָה֙ לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָרִאשׁ֔וֹן יָֽשָׁבְעָ֖ם בֶּן־זַבְדִּיאֵ֑ל וְעַל֙ מַֽחֲלֻקְתּ֔וֹ עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֖ה אָֽלֶף׃
records.gloss: Over the division the first for the month the first [was] Jashobeam son of Zabdiel, and with his division [were] twenty and four thousand.
pieces: In charge of the first division, for the first month, was Jashobeam son of Zabdiel. His division numbered 24,000.

L.2: Over the first division for the first month [was] Jashobeam son of Zabdiel, and in his division [were] 24,000.

R.2: The commander of the first division, for the first month, was Jashobeam son of Zabdiel. His division had 24,000 men.

decisions.choice: Jashobeam: the chief of David's mighty warriors, here called son of Zabdiel
decisions.reason: A Jashobeam heads the list of David's mighty warriors in 11:11, where he is "son of Hachmoni" (in 2 Samuel 23:8 the name is Josheb-Basshebeth the Tahchemonite). Here his father is Zabdiel. Hachmoni may be a family name rather than his father's name, but the text does not say.

decisions.choice: one formula for the twelve divisions
decisions.reason: Verses 2-15 name the commander of each month's division in a fixed pattern, closing each time with the number of men in the division (on the size of the figures see verse 1). Most of the commanders are among David's mighty warriors in 11:10-47.

decisions.choice: one wording for every division: "and in his division [were] 24,000" (Literal); "His division numbered 24,000" (Balanced); "His division had 24,000 men" (Readable)
decisions.reason: The same closing words are kept in all twelve verses so the reader can see the pattern of the Hebrew. Readable says they were men, as in verse 1.

records.source: מִן־בְּנֵי־פֶ֗רֶץ הָרֹ֛אשׁ לְכָל־שָׂרֵ֥י הַצְּבָא֖וֹת לַחֹ֥דֶשׁ הָרִאשֽׁוֹן׃
records.gloss: From [the] sons of Perez, the head of all [the] commanders of the armies for the month the first.
pieces: He was a descendant of Perez and was chief of all the army commanders for the first month.

L.3: From the sons of Perez [he was], the head of all the commanders of the armies for the first month.

R.3: He was from the family of Perez, in the tribe of Judah. He was the head of all the army commanders for the first month.

decisions.choice: the sons of Perez: the leading clan of Judah
decisions.reason: Perez was a son of Judah (Genesis 38:29; 1 Chronicles 2:4-5), and David's own family came from Perez (2:5-15; Ruth 4:18-22). The first commander came from the king's tribe.

decisions.choice: head of all the commanders for the first month: chief over the officers who served that month
decisions.reason: He led all the commanders on duty in his month, as each division's commander did in turn.

decisions.choice: in the tribe of Judah
decisions.reason: Readable says which tribe Perez belonged to (m1).

records.source: וְעַ֞ל מַחֲלֹ֣קֶת׀הַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִ֗י דּוֹדַ֤י הָאֲחוֹחִי֙ וּמַ֣חֲלֻקְתּ֔וֹ וּמִקְל֖וֹת הַנָּגִ֑יד וְעַל֙ מַחֲלֻקְתּ֔וֹ עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֖ה אָֽלֶף׃ס
records.gloss: And over [the] division of the month the second [was] Dodai the Ahohite, and his division, and Mikloth the ruler; and with his division [were] twenty and four thousand.
pieces: In charge of the division for the second month was Dodai the Ahohite, and Mikloth was the chief officer of his division. His division numbered 24,000.

L.4: And over the division of the second month [was] Dodai the Ahohite, and [of] his division Mikloth [was] the ruler; and in his division [were] 24,000.

R.4: For the second month the commander was Dodai the Ahohite, and Mikloth was the leader under him. His division had 24,000 men.

decisions.choice: Dodai the Ahohite: related to Eleazar son of Dodo the Ahohite
alternatives: Eleazar son of Dodai the Ahohite
decisions.reason: In 11:12 and 2 Samuel 23:9 the second of David's mighty warriors is "Eleazar son of Dodo the Ahohite". Dodai is another form of Dodo. Here the father's name stands where the son's might be expected, so either the father commanded this division or the words "Eleazar son of" were lost in copying. The text as it stands names Dodai.

decisions.choice: and his division, Mikloth the ruler: Mikloth was the officer in charge under Dodai
decisions.reason: The words "and his division" stand loosely before Mikloth's name. They are best read as "and of his division, Mikloth was the ruler": an officer second to Dodai, who ran the division day to day.

decisions.choice: the ruler (Literal); the chief officer (Balanced); the leader (Readable)
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for a ruler (1 Samuel 9:16). Literal keeps "ruler" as elsewhere, but for an officer within one army division Balanced says "chief officer", since "ruler" would suggest he governed a land.

records.source: שַׂ֣ר הַצָּבָ֤א הַשְּׁלִישִׁי֙ לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֔י בְּנָיָ֧הוּ בֶן־יְהוֹיָדָ֛ע הַכֹּהֵ֖ן רֹ֑אשׁ וְעַל֙ מַחֲלֻקְתּ֔וֹ עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֖ה אָֽלֶף׃
records.gloss: [The] commander of the army the third for the month the third [was] Benaiah son of Jehoiada the priest, chief; and with his division [were] twenty and four thousand.
pieces: The third army commander, for the third month, was Benaiah son of Jehoiada the priest, who served as chief. His division numbered 24,000.

L.5: The third commander of the army, for the third month, [was] Benaiah son of Jehoiada the priest, [as] chief; and in his division [were] 24,000.

R.5: For the third month the army commander was Benaiah, whose father was Jehoiada the priest. Benaiah was a chief commander. His division had 24,000 men.

decisions.choice: Benaiah son of Jehoiada: David's warrior, captain of the bodyguard
decisions.reason: This is the Benaiah of 11:22-25 and 2 Samuel 23:20-23, whom David put in charge of his bodyguard (18:17). Only here and in 12:28 is his father Jehoiada called a priest; 12:28 names a Jehoiada as the leader of the family of Aaron.

decisions.choice: chief: describing Benaiah, who was a chief or head
alternatives: Benaiah son of Jehoiada the chief priest
decisions.reason: The word "chief" stands alone after "the priest". It can be read as part of Jehoiada's title, "Jehoiada the chief priest", but the accents set it apart, and it is read here as saying that Benaiah held the rank of chief.

decisions.choice: who served as chief
decisions.reason: Balanced supplies "who served as" to make the single word "chief" read as a description of Benaiah (m2).

records.source: ה֧וּא בְנָיָ֛הוּ גִּבּ֥וֹר הַשְּׁלֹשִׁ֖ים וְעַל־הַשְּׁלֹשִׁ֑ים וּמַ֣חֲלֻקְתּ֔וֹ עַמִּיזָבָ֖ד בְּנֽוֹ׃ס
records.gloss: That [is] Benaiah, mighty [man] of the Thirty and over the Thirty; and his division: Ammizabad his son.
pieces: This was the Benaiah who was a mighty warrior among the Thirty and was over the Thirty. His son Ammizabad was in charge of his division.

L.6: That [was] Benaiah, a mighty man of the Thirty and over the Thirty; and [over] his division [was] Ammizabad his son.

R.6: This Benaiah was one of the Thirty, David's best warriors, and he was also their leader. His son Ammizabad was in charge of his division.

decisions.choice: a mighty man of the Thirty and over the Thirty
decisions.reason: In 11:25 and 2 Samuel 23:23 Benaiah is "honored above the Thirty", the group of David's chief warriors (11:11, 15). Here he is also "over the Thirty", their commander.

decisions.choice: his division, Ammizabad his son: Ammizabad led the division, under or after his father
decisions.reason: The words name Ammizabad as the one in charge of the division without a verb. Since Benaiah also commanded the bodyguard (18:17), his son may have led the division for him, or after him, as Zebadiah followed Asahel (verse 7).

decisions.choice: the Thirty (capital T)
decisions.reason: As in 11:11, the name of the group of warriors is written with a capital letter.

decisions.choice: David's best warriors
decisions.reason: Readable says who the Thirty were (11:11, 15).

records.source: הָֽרְבִיעִ֞י לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָרְבִיעִ֗י עֲשָׂה־אֵל֙ אֲחִ֣י יוֹאָ֔ב וּזְבַדְיָ֥ה בְנ֖וֹ אַחֲרָ֑יו וְעַל֙ מַחֲלֻקְתּ֔וֹ עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֖ה אָֽלֶף׃ס
records.gloss: The fourth for the month the fourth [was] Asahel brother of Joab, and Zebadiah his son after him; and with his division [were] twenty and four thousand.
pieces: The fourth commander, for the fourth month, was Asahel the brother of Joab, and after him his son Zebadiah. His division numbered 24,000.

L.7: The fourth, for the fourth month, [was] Asahel the brother of Joab, and Zebadiah his son after him; and in his division [were] 24,000.

R.7: For the fourth month the commander was Asahel the brother of Joab, and after him his son Zebadiah. His division had 24,000 men.

decisions.choice: Asahel the brother of Joab, followed by his son Zebadiah
decisions.reason: Asahel heads the list of the Thirty in 11:26 and 2 Samuel 23:24. He was killed by Abner while David reigned in Hebron (2 Samuel 2:18-23), so his son taking the command "after him" fits the story. The list may name the division after its first commander.

decisions.choice: commander
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "the fourth", "the fifth" and so on; the word "commander" is understood from verses 2-5. Balanced and Readable supply it.

records.source: הַחַמִישִׁי֙ לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַחֲמִישִׁ֔י הַשַּׂ֖ר שַׁמְה֣וּת הַיִּזְרָ֑ח וְעַל֙ מַחֲלֻקְתּ֔וֹ עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֖ה אָֽלֶף׃ס
records.gloss: The fifth for the month the fifth [was] the commander Shamhuth the Izrahite; and with his division [were] twenty and four thousand.
pieces: The fifth commander, for the fifth month, was Shamhuth the Izrahite. His division numbered 24,000.

L.8: The fifth, for the fifth month, [was] the commander Shamhuth the Izrahite; and in his division [were] 24,000.

R.8: For the fifth month the commander was Shamhuth the Izrahite. His division had 24,000 men.

decisions.choice: Shamhuth the Izrahite: probably Shammoth the Harorite of 11:27
decisions.reason: The name is close to Shammoth the Harorite (11:27) and Shammah the Harodite (2 Samuel 23:25). "Izrahite" may mean a member of the clan of Zerah (verses 11, 13). The forms differ, and it is not certain that the same man is meant.

decisions.choice: commander
decisions.reason: As in verse 7; here the Hebrew has the word "commander" before the name, which Balanced and Readable move to its place in the pattern.

records.source: הַשִּׁשִּׁי֙ לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשִּׁשִּׁ֔י עִירָ֥א בֶן־עִקֵּ֖שׁ הַתְּקוֹעִ֑י וְעַל֙ מַחֲלֻקְתּ֔וֹ עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֖ה אָֽלֶף׃ס
records.gloss: The sixth for the month the sixth [was] Ira son of Ikkesh the Tekoite; and with his division [were] twenty and four thousand.
pieces: The sixth commander, for the sixth month, was Ira son of Ikkesh the Tekoite. His division numbered 24,000.

L.9: The sixth, for the sixth month, [was] Ira son of Ikkesh the Tekoite; and in his division [were] 24,000.

R.9: For the sixth month the commander was Ira son of Ikkesh the Tekoite. His division had 24,000 men.

decisions.choice: Ira son of Ikkesh the Tekoite: as in 11:28 and 2 Samuel 23:26
decisions.reason: One of David's mighty warriors, from Tekoa in Judah, south of Bethlehem.

decisions.choice: commander
decisions.reason: As in verse 7.

records.source: הַשְּׁבִיעִי֙ לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י חֶ֥לֶץ הַפְּלוֹנִ֖י מִן־בְּנֵ֣י אֶפְרָ֑יִם וְעַל֙ מַחֲלֻקְתּ֔וֹ עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֖ה אָֽלֶף׃ס
records.gloss: The seventh for the month the seventh [was] Helez the Pelonite from [the] sons of Ephraim; and with his division [were] twenty and four thousand.
pieces: The seventh commander, for the seventh month, was Helez the Pelonite, an Ephraimite. His division numbered 24,000.

L.10: The seventh, for the seventh month, [was] Helez the Pelonite, from the sons of Ephraim; and in his division [were] 24,000.

R.10: For the seventh month the commander was Helez the Pelonite, from the tribe of Ephraim. His division had 24,000 men.

decisions.choice: Helez the Pelonite: as in 11:27; "the Paltite" in 2 Samuel 23:26
decisions.reason: The same warrior. Here the list adds that he was from the tribe of Ephraim.

decisions.choice: commander
decisions.reason: As in verse 7.

records.source: הַשְּׁמִינִי֙ לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשְּׁמִינִ֔י סִבְּכַ֥י הַחֻשָׁתִ֖י לַזַּרְחִ֑י וְעַל֙ מַחֲלֻקְתּ֔וֹ עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֖ה אָֽלֶף׃ס
records.gloss: The eighth for the month the eighth [was] Sibbecai the Hushathite of the Zerahite[s]; and with his division [were] twenty and four thousand.
pieces: The eighth commander, for the eighth month, was Sibbecai the Hushathite, a Zerahite. His division numbered 24,000.

L.11: The eighth, for the eighth month, [was] Sibbecai the Hushathite, of the Zerahites; and in his division [were] 24,000.

R.11: For the eighth month the commander was Sibbecai the Hushathite, from the clan of Zerah. His division had 24,000 men.

decisions.choice: Sibbecai the Hushathite: as in 11:29; "Mebunnai" in 2 Samuel 23:27
decisions.reason: Sibbecai killed one of the giant's descendants (20:4; 2 Samuel 21:18). In the list at 2 Samuel 23:27 the name is written Mebunnai, a difference of a few similar letters.

decisions.choice: the Zerahites: a clan of Judah
decisions.reason: The clan of Zerah, Judah's son and Perez's twin (Genesis 38:30; Numbers 26:20).

decisions.choice: commander
decisions.reason: As in verse 7.

records.source: הַתְּשִׁיעִי֙ לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַתְּשִׁיעִ֔י אֲבִיעֶ֥זֶר הָעַנְּתֹתִ֖י לַבֵּ֣ן׀יְמִינִ֑י וְעַל֙ מַחֲלֻקְתּ֔וֹ עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֖ה אָֽלֶף׃ס
records.gloss: The ninth for the month the ninth [was] Abiezer the Anathothite of the Benjaminite[s]; and with his division [were] twenty and four thousand.
pieces: The ninth commander, for the ninth month, was Abiezer the Anathothite, a Benjaminite. His division numbered 24,000.

L.12: The ninth, for the ninth month, [was] Abiezer the Anathothite, of the Benjaminites; and in his division [were] 24,000.

R.12: For the ninth month the commander was Abiezer the Anathothite, from the tribe of Benjamin. His division had 24,000 men.

decisions.choice: Abiezer the Anathothite: as in 11:28 and 2 Samuel 23:27
decisions.reason: From Anathoth, a town of Benjamin (Joshua 21:18), which is why the list adds "of the Benjaminites".

decisions.choice: Benjaminites
decisions.reason: The Hebrew writes the clan name as two words; it is spelled "Benjaminite" as in 11:31 and 2 Samuel 23:29.

decisions.choice: commander
decisions.reason: As in verse 7.

records.source: הָעֲשִׂירִי֙ לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָעֲשִׂירִ֔י מַהְרַ֥י הַנְּטֽוֹפָתִ֖י לַזַּרְחִ֑י וְעַל֙ מַֽחֲלֻקְתּ֔וֹ עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֖ה אָֽלֶף׃ס
records.gloss: The tenth for the month the tenth [was] Maharai the Netophathite of the Zerahite[s]; and with his division [were] twenty and four thousand.
pieces: The tenth commander, for the tenth month, was Maharai the Netophathite, a Zerahite. His division numbered 24,000.

L.13: The tenth, for the tenth month, [was] Maharai the Netophathite, of the Zerahites; and in his division [were] 24,000.

R.13: For the tenth month the commander was Maharai the Netophathite, from the clan of Zerah. His division had 24,000 men.

decisions.choice: Maharai the Netophathite: as in 11:30 and 2 Samuel 23:28
decisions.reason: From Netophah, near Bethlehem (Ezra 2:22), of the clan of Zerah in Judah (verse 11).

decisions.choice: commander
decisions.reason: As in verse 7.

records.source: עַשְׁתֵּֽי־עָשָׂר֙ לְעַשְׁתֵּ֣י־עָשָׂ֣ר הַחֹ֔דֶשׁ בְּנָיָ֥ה הַפִּרְעָתוֹנִ֖י מִן־בְּנֵ֣י אֶפְרָ֑יִם וְעַל֙ מַחֲלֻקְתּ֔וֹ עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֖ה אָֽלֶף׃ס
records.gloss: [The] eleventh for the eleventh month [was] Benaiah the Pirathonite from [the] sons of Ephraim; and with his division [were] twenty and four thousand.
pieces: The eleventh commander, for the eleventh month, was Benaiah the Pirathonite, an Ephraimite. His division numbered 24,000.

L.14: The eleventh, for the eleventh month, [was] Benaiah the Pirathonite, from the sons of Ephraim; and in his division [were] 24,000.

R.14: For the eleventh month the commander was Benaiah the Pirathonite, from the tribe of Ephraim. His division had 24,000 men.

decisions.choice: Benaiah the Pirathonite: as in 11:31 and 2 Samuel 23:30
decisions.reason: From Pirathon in the hill country of Ephraim (Judges 12:15). He is a different man from Benaiah son of Jehoiada (verse 5).

decisions.choice: one plus ten, the eleventh
decisions.reason: The Hebrew forms "eleventh" as "one and ten", and "twelfth" (verse 15) as "two and ten".

decisions.choice: commander
decisions.reason: As in verse 7.

records.source: הַשְּׁנֵ֤ים עָשָׂר֙ לִשְׁנֵ֣ים עָשָׂ֣ר הַחֹ֔דֶשׁ חֶלְדַּ֥י הַנְּטוֹפָתִ֖י לְעָתְנִיאֵ֑ל וְעַל֙ מַחֲלֻקְתּ֔וֹ עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֖ה אָֽלֶף׃פ
records.gloss: The twelfth for the twelfth month [was] Heldai the Netophathite of Othniel; and with his division [were] twenty and four thousand.
pieces: The twelfth commander, for the twelfth month, was Heldai the Netophathite, of the family of Othniel. His division numbered 24,000.

L.15: The twelfth, for the twelfth month, [was] Heldai the Netophathite, of Othniel; and in his division [were] 24,000.

R.15: For the twelfth month the commander was Heldai the Netophathite, from the family of Othniel. His division had 24,000 men.

decisions.choice: Heldai the Netophathite: Heled son of Baanah in 11:30, Heleb in 2 Samuel 23:29
decisions.reason: The three forms of the name differ by one letter and name the same Netophathite warrior.

decisions.choice: of Othniel: of the family of Othniel, Caleb's kinsman
decisions.reason: Othniel was the first of the judges, from Judah (Judges 1:13; 3:9-11). Heldai belonged to his family.

decisions.choice: commander; of the family of
decisions.reason: As in verse 7; and "of Othniel" is said as "of the family of Othniel".

records.source: וְעַל֙ שִׁבְטֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לָרֽאוּבֵנִ֣י נָגִ֔יד אֱלִיעֶ֖זֶר בֶּן־זִכְרִ֑יסלַשִּׁ֨מְעוֹנִ֔י שְׁפַטְיָ֖הוּ בֶּֽן־מַעֲכָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: And over [the] tribes of Israel: for the Reubenite[s], ruler [was] Eliezer son of Zichri; for the Simeonite[s], Shephatiah son of Maacah;
pieces: Over the tribes of Israel were these: for the Reubenites, the ruler was Eliezer son of Zichri; for the Simeonites, Shephatiah son of Maacah;

L.16: And over the tribes of Israel: for the Reubenites, [the] ruler [was] Eliezer son of Zichri; for the Simeonites, Shephatiah son of Maacah;

R.16: These were the leaders over the tribes of Israel. For the Reubenites it was Eliezer son of Zichri. For the Simeonites it was Shephatiah son of Maacah.

decisions.choice: the rulers of the tribes: a leader over each tribe
decisions.reason: After the army divisions the list names the man set over each tribe (verses 16-22). The word for "ruler" is the one used of a leader appointed over a people (1 Samuel 9:16); here it heads a tribe.

decisions.choice: the tribes listed: Gad and Asher are missing
decisions.reason: The list counts Levi and Aaron separately (verse 17) and the two halves of Manasseh separately (verses 20-21), and it leaves out Gad and Asher. The text gives no reason.

decisions.choice: ruler (Literal, Balanced); leader (Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording kept for this title in Samuel, Kings and Chronicles.

decisions.choice: For the X it was Y
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the list into short sentences, one for each tribe.

records.heading: The leaders of the tribes

records.source: לְלֵוִ֛י חֲשַׁבְיָ֥ה בֶן־קְמוּאֵ֖ל לְאַהֲרֹ֥ן צָדֽוֹק׃ס
records.gloss: for Levi, Hashabiah son of Kemuel; for Aaron, Zadok;
pieces: for Levi, Hashabiah son of Kemuel; for Aaron, Zadok;

L.17: for Levi, Hashabiah son of Kemuel; for Aaron, Zadok;

R.17: For the tribe of Levi it was Hashabiah son of Kemuel. For the descendants of Aaron it was Zadok.

decisions.choice: for Aaron, Zadok: the priests, Aaron's descendants, had their own head
decisions.reason: The priests descended from Aaron are named apart from the rest of Levi. Zadok was one of the two chief priests in David's time (18:16; 24:3).

decisions.choice: the tribe of; the descendants of
decisions.reason: Readable says that Levi is a tribe and that "Aaron" means his descendants, the priests.

records.source: לִֽיהוּדָ֕ה אֱלִיה֖וּ מֵאֲחֵ֣י דָוִ֑יד לְיִ֨שָׂשכָ֔ר עָמְרִ֖י בֶּן־מִיכָאֵֽל׃ס
records.gloss: for Judah, Elihu, from [the] brothers of David; for Issachar, Omri son of Michael;
pieces: for Judah, Elihu, one of David's brothers; for Issachar, Omri son of Michael;

L.18: for Judah, Elihu, [one] of the brothers of David; for Issachar, Omri son of Michael;

R.18: For Judah it was Elihu, one of David's brothers. For Issachar it was Omri son of Michael.

decisions.choice: Elihu, one of David's brothers: perhaps Eliab, his eldest brother
decisions.reason: No brother of David named Elihu appears in the lists of Jesse's sons (2:13-15; 1 Samuel 16:6-10). The name may be another form of Eliab, the eldest. The word "brothers" can also mean relatives in a wider sense.

records.source: לִזְבוּלֻ֕ן יִֽשְׁמַֽעְיָ֖הוּ בֶּן־עֹבַדְיָ֑הוּ לְנַ֨פְתָּלִ֔י יְרִימ֖וֹת בֶּן־עַזְרִיאֵֽל׃ס
records.gloss: for Zebulun, Ishmaiah son of Obadiah; for Naphtali, Jerimoth son of Azriel;
pieces: for Zebulun, Ishmaiah son of Obadiah; for Naphtali, Jerimoth son of Azriel;

L.19: for Zebulun, Ishmaiah son of Obadiah; for Naphtali, Jerimoth son of Azriel;

R.19: For Zebulun it was Ishmaiah son of Obadiah. For Naphtali it was Jerimoth son of Azriel.

decisions.choice: Zebulun, Naphtali: as in verse 16
decisions.reason: The list of tribal leaders goes on in the same pattern.

records.source: לִבְנֵ֣י אֶפְרַ֔יִם הוֹשֵׁ֖עַ בֶּן־עֲזַזְיָ֑הוּ לַחֲצִי֙ שֵׁ֣בֶט מְנַשֶּׁ֔ה יוֹאֵ֖ל בֶּן־פְּדָיָֽהוּ׃ס
records.gloss: for [the] sons of Ephraim, Hoshea son of Azaziah; for half [the] tribe of Manasseh, Joel son of Pedaiah;
pieces: for the Ephraimites, Hoshea son of Azaziah; for the half-tribe of Manasseh, Joel son of Pedaiah;

L.20: for the sons of Ephraim, Hoshea son of Azaziah; for the half tribe of Manasseh, Joel son of Pedaiah;

R.20: For the people of Ephraim it was Hoshea son of Azaziah. For half of the tribe of Manasseh it was Joel son of Pedaiah.

decisions.choice: half the tribe of Manasseh: the half living west of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Manasseh had land on both sides of the Jordan (Joshua 13:29-31; 17:1-13). This half is set against the half "in Gilead", east of the Jordan (verse 21).

records.source: לַחֲצִ֤י הַֽמְנַשֶּׁה֙ גִּלְעָ֔דָה יִדּ֖וֹ בֶּן־זְכַרְיָ֑הוּסלְבִנְיָמִ֔ן יַעֲשִׂיאֵ֖ל בֶּן־אַבְנֵֽר׃ס
records.gloss: for half the Manasseh to Gilead, Iddo son of Zechariah; for Benjamin, Jaasiel son of Abner;
pieces: for the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead, Iddo son of Zechariah; for Benjamin, Jaasiel son of Abner;

L.21: for the half of Manasseh in Gilead, Iddo son of Zechariah; for Benjamin, Jaasiel son of Abner;

R.21: For the half of Manasseh that lived in Gilead it was Iddo son of Zechariah. For Benjamin it was Jaasiel son of Abner.

decisions.choice: the half of Manasseh in Gilead: east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Gilead is the highland east of the Jordan, where half of Manasseh settled (Numbers 32:39-42).

decisions.choice: Jaasiel son of Abner: perhaps the son of Saul's commander
decisions.reason: Abner, Saul's army commander, was a Benjaminite and Saul's relative (1 Samuel 14:50-51). The text does not say that this Abner is the same man.

records.source: לְדָ֕ן עֲזַרְאֵ֖ל בֶּן־יְרֹחָ֑ם אֵ֕לֶּה שָׂרֵ֖י שִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: for Dan, Azarel son of Jeroham. These [were the] princes of [the] tribes of Israel.
pieces: for Dan, Azarel son of Jeroham. These were the leaders over Israel's tribes.

L.22: for Dan, Azarel son of Jeroham. These [were] the princes of the tribes of Israel.

R.22: For Dan it was Azarel son of Jeroham. These men led the tribes of Israel.

decisions.choice: princes: the men in charge of the tribes
decisions.reason: The word is the common title for an official or leader under the king. Here it sums up the men just named as heads of the tribes (verse 16).

decisions.choice: leaders (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "princes" as usual for this word. For the heads of tribes Balanced says "leaders" rather than "officials", which fits a tribe better.

records.source: וְלֹא־נָשָׂ֤א דָוִיד֙ מִסְפָּרָ֔ם לְמִבֶּ֛ן עֶשְׂרִ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה וּלְמָ֑טָּה כִּ֚י אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה לְהַרְבּ֥וֹת אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל כְּכוֹכְבֵ֥י הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And not took David their number from [a] son of twenty year[s] and below, for had said Yahweh to multiply Israel like [the] stars of the heavens.
pieces: David did not count those who were twenty years old or younger, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had promised to make Israel as many as the stars in the sky.

L.23: And David did not take their number from twenty years old and below, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said to multiply Israel like the stars of the heavens.

R.23: David did not count the men who were twenty years old or younger. This was because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had promised to make the people of Israel as many as the stars in the sky.

decisions.choice: to multiply Israel like the stars of the heavens: the promise to Abraham
decisions.reason: The LORD promised Abraham descendants as many as the stars (Genesis 15:5; 22:17), and repeated it to Isaac (Genesis 26:4). Moses recalls it in Exodus 32:13 and Deuteronomy 1:10. A people God had promised to make countless was not to be counted in full.

decisions.choice: from twenty and below: those too young for military service
decisions.reason: Men were counted for the army from twenty years old and up (Numbers 1:3). David's count, like Moses' census, covered only men of fighting age.

decisions.choice: had said: had promised
decisions.reason: The verb "say" here refers to what the LORD had declared he would do, a promise.

decisions.choice: the men
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that "those" counted were the men, as in verse 1.

records.source: יוֹאָ֨ב בֶּן־צְרוּיָ֜ה הֵחֵ֤ל לִמְנוֹת֙ וְלֹ֣א כִלָּ֔ה וַיְהִ֥י בָזֹ֛את קֶ֖צֶף עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְלֹ֤א עָלָה֙ הַמִּסְפָּ֔ר בְּמִסְפַּ֥ר דִּבְרֵֽי־הַיָּמִ֖ים לַמֶּ֥לֶךְ דָּוִֽיד׃ס
records.gloss: Joab son of Zeruiah began to count, and not he finished; and was because of this wrath upon Israel, and not went up the number in [the] number of [the] matters of the days of the king David.
pieces: Joab son of Zeruiah began to count them but did not finish. Because of this, wrath came on Israel, and the number was not entered in the record of the History of King David.

L.24: Joab son of Zeruiah began to count, and he did not finish; and there was wrath on Israel because of this, and the number did not go up into the account of the matters of the days of King David.

R.24: Joab son of Zeruiah started to count the men, but he did not finish. Because of the count, God's anger came on Israel. So the total was never written down in the history of King David's reign.

decisions.choice: Joab began to count but did not finish; wrath came: the census of chapter 21
decisions.reason: This is the count David ordered in 21:1-6, which Joab carried out against his will and left unfinished, not counting Levi and Benjamin (21:6). God was displeased and struck Israel with a plague (21:7, 14; 2 Samuel 24:1, 15).

decisions.choice: wrath: God's anger against the census
decisions.reason: The word is used for God's anger at sin (Numbers 1:53; 18:5). The verse does not name God, but chapter 21 shows that the anger was his.

decisions.choice: the account of the matters of the days of King David: the royal record of David's reign
decisions.reason: This is the kind of official court record that Kings and Chronicles cite as a source (1 Kings 14:19). Here the word for "number" or "account" stands where those formulas have "book", and the record is David's own. It has not survived, and it is not the biblical book of Chronicles.

decisions.choice: the record of the History of King David (Balanced); the history of King David's reign (Readable)
decisions.reason: The source formula is "the Book of the History of the Kings of Israel" at Balanced and "the history of the kings of Israel" at Readable (1 Kings 14:19). It is adapted here: "record" for the Hebrew word "account", and King David in place of the kings of Israel.

decisions.choice: the men; God's anger
decisions.reason: Readable says who was counted and whose anger it was (m2).

records.source: וְעַל֙ אֹצְר֣וֹת הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ עַזְמָ֖וֶת בֶּן־עֲדִיאֵ֑לסוְעַ֣ל הָֽאֹצָר֡וֹת בַּשָּׂדֶ֞ה בֶּעָרִ֤ים וּבַכְּפָרִים֙ וּבַמִּגְדָּל֔וֹת יְהוֹנָתָ֖ן בֶּן־עֻזִּיָּֽהוּ׃ס
records.gloss: And over [the] treasuries of the king [was] Azmaveth son of Adiel; and over the treasuries in the field, in the cities and in the villages and in the towers, [was] Jonathan son of Uzziah.
pieces: Azmaveth son of Adiel was in charge of the king's treasuries. Jonathan son of Uzziah was in charge of the storehouses out in the country, in the towns, in the villages and in the towers.

L.25: And over the treasuries of the king [was] Azmaveth son of Adiel; and over the treasuries in the field, in the cities and in the villages and in the towers, [was] Jonathan son of Uzziah.

R.25: Azmaveth son of Adiel was in charge of the king's treasures. The storehouses in the countryside, the towns, the villages and the watchtowers were under Jonathan son of Uzziah.

decisions.choice: treasuries: stores of the king's wealth and goods
decisions.reason: The same word is used for both. The first is the king's own treasury, at the palace; the second is the network of storehouses across the land where produce and supplies were kept (2 Chronicles 32:27-28).

decisions.choice: towers: fortified posts in the countryside
decisions.reason: Towers guarded farmland and herds and served as stores (2 Chronicles 26:10; 27:4).

decisions.choice: the king's stewards: verses 25-31
decisions.reason: The list now turns from the army and the tribes to the men who managed the king's own lands, crops and animals (verse 31).

decisions.choice: treasuries ... storehouses (Balanced); treasures ... storehouses (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps one word for the one Hebrew word. Balanced and Readable use "storehouses" for the stores across the countryside (m1).

records.heading: The managers of the king's property

records.source: וְעַ֗ל עֹשֵׂי֙ מְלֶ֣אכֶת הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה לַעֲבֹדַ֖ת הָאֲדָמָ֑ה עֶזְרִ֖י בֶּן־כְּלֽוּב׃
records.gloss: And over [the] doers of [the] work of the field for [the] labor of the ground [was] Ezri son of Chelub.
pieces: Ezri son of Chelub was in charge of the field workers who farmed the land.

L.26: And over the doers of the work of the field, for the labor of the ground, [was] Ezri son of Chelub.

R.26: Ezri son of Chelub was in charge of the workers who farmed the king's land.

decisions.choice: the doers of the work of the field for the labor of the ground: the farm workers
decisions.reason: The phrase describes the men who worked the royal farmland, plowing and sowing.

decisions.choice: the king's land
decisions.reason: Readable says whose land it was; the whole list is of King David's property (verse 31).

records.source: וְעַל־הַ֨כְּרָמִ֔ים שִׁמְעִ֖י הָרָֽמָתִ֑י וְעַ֤ל שֶׁבַּכְּרָמִים֙ לְאֹצְר֣וֹת הַיַּ֔יִן זַבְדִּ֖י הַשִּׁפְמִֽי׃ס
records.gloss: And over the vineyards [was] Shimei the Ramathite; and over what [was] in the vineyards for [the] storehouses of the wine [was] Zabdi the Shiphmite.
pieces: Shimei the Ramathite was in charge of the vineyards, and Zabdi the Shiphmite was in charge of the vineyards' yield for the wine cellars.

L.27: And over the vineyards [was] Shimei the Ramathite; and over what [was] in the vineyards, for the storehouses of the wine, [was] Zabdi the Shiphmite.

R.27: Shimei the Ramathite looked after the vineyards. Zabdi the Shiphmite was responsible for storing the wine they produced.

decisions.choice: what was in the vineyards for the storehouses of wine: the grapes and wine to be stored
decisions.reason: One man oversaw the vines; another oversaw their yield, the wine that went into the king's stores.

decisions.choice: the Ramathite, the Shiphmite: named by their home towns
decisions.reason: A Ramathite came from Ramah, a name several towns bore. Shiphmite may refer to Shepham (Numbers 34:10-11), or to another place now unknown.

decisions.choice: wine cellars (Balanced); storing the wine (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Storehouses of wine" said in plain words.

records.source: וְעַל־הַזֵּיתִ֤ים וְהַשִּׁקְמִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּשְּׁפֵלָ֔ה בַּ֥עַל חָנָ֖ן הַגְּדֵרִ֑יסוְעַל־אֹצְר֥וֹת הַשֶּׁ֖מֶן יוֹעָֽשׁ׃ס
records.gloss: And over the olive trees and the sycamores that [were] in the Shephelah [was] Baal-hanan the Gederite; and over [the] storehouses of the oil [was] Joash.
pieces: Baal-hanan the Gederite was in charge of the olive trees and the sycamore-fig trees in the Shephelah, and Joash was in charge of the stores of olive oil.

L.28: And over the olive trees and the sycamores that [were] in the Shephelah [was] Baal-hanan the Gederite; and over the storehouses of the oil [was] Joash.

R.28: Baal-hanan the Gederite was in charge of the olive trees and the fig trees in the western foothills. Joash was in charge of storing the olive oil.

decisions.choice: sycamores: the sycamore-fig, grown for its fruit and wood
decisions.reason: This tree is a kind of fig, not the sycamore of Europe or America. It grew plentifully in the low hills (1 Kings 10:27), and its fruit and timber were valuable (Amos 7:14; Isaiah 9:9).

decisions.choice: the Shephelah: the low hills between Judah's hill country and the coastal plain
decisions.reason: The name means "lowland". It was good land for olives and figs.

decisions.choice: sycamore-fig trees, the Shephelah (Balanced); fig trees, the western foothills (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 10:27.

records.source: וְעַל־הַבָּקָר֙ הָרֹעִ֣ים בַּשָּׁר֔וֹן שִׁרְטַ֖י הַשָּׁרוֹנִ֑י וְעַל־הַבָּקָר֙ בָּֽעֲמָקִ֔ים שָׁפָ֖ט בֶּן־עַדְלָֽי׃ס
records.gloss: And over the cattle grazing in Sharon [was] Shitrai the Sharonite; and over the cattle in the valleys [was] Shaphat son of Adlai.
pieces: Shitrai the Sharonite was in charge of the herds that grazed in Sharon, and Shaphat son of Adlai over the herds in the valleys.

L.29: And over the cattle that grazed in Sharon [was] Shitrai the Sharonite; and over the cattle in the valleys [was] Shaphat son of Adlai.

R.29: Shitrai from Sharon was in charge of the cattle that grazed in the plain of Sharon. Shaphat son of Adlai was in charge of the cattle in the valleys.

decisions.choice: Shitrai: the reading the scribes marked to be read aloud
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew letters give the name as Shirtai; the scribes' marginal note reads Shitrai. The two differ only in the order of two letters. The spoken reading is followed.

decisions.choice: Sharon: the coastal plain north of Joppa
decisions.reason: Sharon was rich pastureland (Isaiah 65:10).

decisions.choice: the plain of Sharon
decisions.reason: Readable says what kind of place Sharon was.

records.source: וְעַל־הַ֨גְּמַלִּ֔ים אוֹבִ֖יל הַיִּשְׁמְעֵלִ֑י וְעַל־הָ֣אֲתֹנ֔וֹת יֶחְדְּיָ֖הוּ הַמֵּרֹנֹתִֽי׃ס
records.gloss: And over the camels [was] Obil the Ishmaelite; and over the female donkeys [was] Jehdeiah the Meronothite.
pieces: Obil the Ishmaelite was in charge of the camels, and Jehdeiah the Meronothite was in charge of the donkeys.

L.30: And over the camels [was] Obil the Ishmaelite; and over the female donkeys [was] Jehdeiah the Meronothite.

R.30: Obil the Ishmaelite looked after the camels. Jehdeiah the Meronothite looked after the donkeys.

decisions.choice: Obil the Ishmaelite: a man from a people known for camels
decisions.reason: The Ishmaelites were desert traders who traveled with camels (Genesis 37:25). An Ishmaelite was a fitting choice to keep the king's camels.

decisions.choice: female donkeys: the donkeys kept for breeding and milk
decisions.reason: The word means she-donkeys, the most valued part of a herd (Job 1:3; 42:12).

decisions.choice: the donkeys
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say simply "donkeys"; Literal keeps "female".

records.source: וְעַל־הַצֹּ֖אן יָזִ֣יז הַֽהַגְרִ֑י כָּל־אֵ֨לֶּה֙ שָׂרֵ֣י הָרְכ֔וּשׁ אֲשֶׁ֖ר לַמֶּ֥לֶךְ דָּוִֽיד׃
records.gloss: And over the flock [was] Jaziz the Hagrite. All these [were] officials of the property that [belonged] to the king David.
pieces: Jaziz the Hagrite was in charge of the flocks. All these were the officials in charge of King David's property.

L.31: And over the flock [was] Jaziz the Hagrite. All these [were] princes of the property that [belonged] to King David.

R.31: Jaziz the Hagrite was in charge of the sheep and goats. All these men managed the property that belonged to King David.

decisions.choice: Jaziz the Hagrite: from a people of the eastern desert
decisions.reason: The Hagrites were herders east of Gilead, defeated by the eastern tribes in Saul's day (5:10, 19-22). Like Obil (verse 30), this herdsman was not an Israelite.

decisions.choice: officials: officers in charge
decisions.reason: The word, often "princes", is the general title for an official under the king. Here it names the stewards over the royal property.

decisions.choice: princes (Literal); officials (Balanced); managed (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "princes" for this word, as elsewhere (28:1); the word names men of rank under the king, here the stewards of his property (m2). Balanced says "officials", and Readable says what they did.

decisions.choice: the sheep and goats
decisions.reason: The word for "flock" covers both sheep and goats.

records.source: וִֽיהוֹנָתָ֤ן דּוֹד־דָּוִיד֙ יוֹעֵ֔ץ אִישׁ־מֵבִ֥ין וְסוֹפֵ֖ר ה֑וּא וִֽיחִיאֵ֥ל בֶּן־חַכְמוֹנִ֖י עִם־בְּנֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃
records.gloss: And Jonathan uncle of David [was a] counselor, [a] man understanding, and [a] scribe [was] he; and Jehiel son of Hachmoni [was] with the sons of the king.
pieces: Jonathan, David's uncle, was a counselor; he was a man of understanding and a scribe. Jehiel son of Hachmoni attended the king's sons.

L.32: And Jonathan, David's uncle, [was] a counselor, a man of understanding, and he [was] a scribe; and Jehiel son of Hachmoni [was] with the king's sons.

R.32: Jonathan, David's uncle, was an adviser to the king. He was a wise man and a scribe. Jehiel son of Hachmoni took care of the king's sons.

decisions.choice: uncle: the brother of David's father
decisions.reason: The word usually means a father's brother (1 Samuel 10:14). It can also mean a relative more broadly. A Jonathan son of Shimea, David's nephew, is named in 20:7.

decisions.choice: counselor, scribe: an adviser to the king and a man of learning
decisions.reason: A counselor gave the king advice on what to do (2 Samuel 16:23). A scribe could read and write, and kept records; the word can also name the royal secretary (18:16).

decisions.choice: with the king's sons: their attendant or tutor
decisions.reason: Jehiel was assigned to the king's sons, most likely to care for and teach them.

decisions.choice: attended (Balanced); took care of (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only that he was "with" them; Balanced and Readable say it as a task (m3).

records.source: וַאֲחִיתֹ֖פֶל יוֹעֵ֣ץ לַמֶּ֑לֶךְסוְחוּשַׁ֥י הָאַרְכִּ֖י רֵ֥עַ הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃
records.gloss: And Ahithophel [was a] counselor to the king; and Hushai the Archite [was the] friend of the king.
pieces: Ahithophel was counselor to the king, and Hushai the Archite was the king's friend.

L.33: And Ahithophel [was] a counselor to the king; and Hushai the Archite [was] the friend of the king.

R.33: Ahithophel was the king's adviser. Hushai the Archite was the king's friend, his trusted adviser.

decisions.choice: Ahithophel the king's counselor: as in 2 Samuel 15:12
decisions.reason: Ahithophel of Giloh is called "David's counselor" in 2 Samuel 15:12. His advice was treated like a word from God (2 Samuel 16:23), but he joined Absalom's revolt and, when his advice was not followed, took his own life (2 Samuel 17:23).

decisions.choice: the friend of the king: a court title for the king's confidant
decisions.reason: "The king's friend" was a position at court, a trusted adviser (1 Kings 4:5). Hushai is "David's friend" in 2 Samuel 15:37 and 16:16, where he defeated Ahithophel's advice (2 Samuel 17:14).

decisions.choice: the Archite: from the Archite clan near Bethel
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 15:32; the Archites lived on the border of Ephraim and Benjamin (Joshua 16:2).

decisions.choice: his trusted adviser
decisions.reason: Readable says what the title "the king's friend" meant (m2).

decisions.choice: adviser
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 15:12, Readable says "adviser" for "counselor".

records.source: וְאַחֲרֵ֣י אֲחִיתֹ֗פֶל יְהוֹיָדָ֤ע בֶּן־בְּנָיָ֨הוּ֙ וְאֶבְיָתָ֔ר וְשַׂר־צָבָ֥א לַמֶּ֖לֶךְ יוֹאָֽב׃פ
records.gloss: And after Ahithophel [were] Jehoiada son of Benaiah and Abiathar; and [the] commander of [the] army of the king [was] Joab.
pieces: After Ahithophel came Jehoiada son of Benaiah and Abiathar. Joab was the commander of the king's army.

L.34: And after Ahithophel [were] Jehoiada son of Benaiah and Abiathar; and the commander of the army of the king [was] Joab.

R.34: After Ahithophel, Jehoiada son of Benaiah and Abiathar became the king's advisers. Joab was the commander of the king's army.

decisions.choice: after Ahithophel: they succeeded him as counselors
decisions.reason: After Ahithophel joined Absalom and died (2 Samuel 17:23), these men took his place as the king's advisers.

decisions.choice: Jehoiada son of Benaiah: perhaps a son of Benaiah named after his grandfather
decisions.reason: Elsewhere Benaiah is the son of Jehoiada (verse 5). This Jehoiada may be Benaiah's son, named after his grandfather, or the two names may have been reversed in copying.

decisions.choice: Abiathar; Joab: the priest and the commander of David's army
decisions.reason: Abiathar was the priest who escaped Saul's slaughter at Nob and stayed with David (1 Samuel 22:20-23; 2 Samuel 15:24-29). Joab son of Zeruiah was commander of the army (18:15).

decisions.choice: became the king's advisers
decisions.reason: Readable says what "after Ahithophel" means (m1).

decisions.choice: the commander of the king's army
decisions.reason: The wording for this title in Samuel, Kings and Chronicles; the Hebrew here adds "of the king".
